# C01 — Subject / Defined Indefinability

## #0

**The Subject is that to which an appearance is present, without itself becoming one more appearance alongside it.** A thought, a remembered scene, an ache, an act of judgment and the thought “this is me” can each become something known. Their being known already involves the Subject. Adding that involvement to the description produces a further known relation; it does not put the one to whom the description appears inside it as another item.

This is intimate before it is theoretical. I can question a memory, revise my identity, fail to recognise myself in a portrait, or discover that an apparent certainty was mistaken. The questioning, failure and discovery are nevertheless present. What is at issue is not whether my description of myself is correct, but the presence within which correctness and error matter at all. Taylor's *Definition of God*, in its return to Zero, puts the pressure directly: “I am undeniable, though nowhere to be seen.” The word *I* here does not certify everything I say about myself. It names the first-person presence which an account of those sayings already enacts.

To [define the Subject faithfully](../A01-Subject-God-and-Faithful-Definition.md) is to distinguish the presence to which something is given from the something given, including every representation of that presence. The defining act is itself present; its account becomes one more determination within that presence. This difference remains active when the inquiry turns from the predicates of God to a memory, self-image or report.

The finding can be stated in its fact/contents form. The fact of first-person immediacy is undeniable by definition: any denial of it is performed in the presence it denies. Its contents are not. A thought, a doubting, a self-image — and the thinking-thing a *res cogitans* names — remain determinate occurrences within that presence, corrigible like every determination. The classical reification converted the condition of appearing into one more appearance and then treated that conversion as capture of the condition; the essay's crossed zero names the resulting occlusion `Ø`. Denying the fact is impossible; reifying it is the opposite error; defined indefinability holds both edges at once.

## #1

**Defined indefinability** positively determines this asymmetry. It does not mean that the Subject is obscure because the correct description has not yet been found. It means that any description, however exact, remains a determination *for* the subject-pole it seeks to describe. The definition states why exhaustive objectification changes the office of its referent: it converts the condition of appearing into an appearance and then treats that conversion as capture of the condition.

A biography can identify a particular person. A physiological account can identify conditions of an experience. An introspective account can describe what that experience feels like. None becomes worthless because it does not exhaust the Subject. Each becomes more exact when it states what it determines and does not promote that determination into the whole reality of the one concerned. An account [determines through a cut](C03-Determination.md): it selects, excludes and relates. Its [fidelity](C02-Faithful-Definition.md) keeps that selection answerable to the person or appearing it concerns.

The difference is between *I am* and *I am this*, not between a meaningful statement and silence. The second can be true: I am this person, speaking here, with this history and concern. It becomes false in office when *this* is made to exhaust the *am* through which the identification is lived. In [identification through difference](../A02-Copula-Self-Identity-through-Difference.md), the person, predicate and circumstance remain related. An identifying predicate can state an identity while the present act in which identification occurs remains its condition.

## #2

Several things usually called “self” must therefore remain distinguishable. **Selfing** is an activity of appropriation: a changing determination is taken as mine, joined to the claim of what I am, and installed as the owner of the field. The **self-thing** is that determination treated as self-subsisting ground. A **bounded self**, by contrast, is a real situated horizon: this embodied life, with its history, limitations and capacity to be addressed. Its dependence does not make it unreal. **Subjectivity-as-such** names the unobjectifiable determining presence, while the capitalised **Self**, in this project's full symbolic use, names the whole relation of Subject and its objective internality, not the Subject isolated from manifestation.

Through [selfing and its acquired image](C35-Selfing-Self-Subjectivity-Self-Thing.md), a life becomes named, remembered and addressable. Exposing a fabricated self-thing does not abolish the presence in which its fabrication is recognised. Conversely, affirming the Subject does not restore the self-thing as an invisible proprietor behind appearances. Neither the image nor an imagined owner of the image can occupy this place.

In Taylor's [Watson encounter](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/psychology/watson/watson-1998-resonance-of-emptiness/watson-1998-resonance-of-emptiness.md), the critique of selfing reaches its object while retaining the experient to whom that critique appears. A changing transactional formation can be recognised as selfing, instead of being grasped as permanent, partless and autonomous. Taylor develops the further positive distinction between that formation and the Subject. Watson's Buddhist–psychotherapeutic comparison concerns the constructed self-world; Taylor carries recognition of that construction into the relation between the determinate formation and the experient.

## #3

The Subject is not an inert witness placed behind a finished display. Knowing that I am does not first require an image of an unknown possessor and then a second observer who recognises it. It is present in the act of knowing. The reflexive relation is intrinsic to appearing; otherwise a luminous display would remain unexperienced, like a reflection that no one sees.

In [luminous self-apprehension](../A05-Prakasa-Vimarsa.md), appearing and its knowing belong to one act. [Dyczkowski's Śaiva account](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/indian-philosophy/dyczkowski/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration/dyczkowski-2000-doctrine-vibration.md), in the available page-labelled discussion around p.70, distinguishes that reflective awareness from an insentient mirror or crystal. The crystal displays a reflected blue; its display is not its recognition of blue. Taylor's comparison brings this operation into defined indefinability: the one knowing the appearance remains present through the knowing, while an image of that one is another appearance. The Śaiva distinction between luminous appearing and reflective awareness makes self-apprehension active; defined indefinability keeps the present act distinct from every image made of it.

The full QL field prevents this relation from freezing into an isolated pair. Its parent `/ = −/−` opens a determinate circumstance as `0/1`; `?/!` makes appearing answerable in question and assertion; `−/+` gives differentiation force; `X/x` distinguishes determining capacity from its local instance; `AM/IS` makes the relation personed and contextual; `∞/dx` retains exact local difference within inexhaustible depth; `1/0` returns the achieved determination toward its condition. The eight turns traverse the sixfold body; they are not eight interchangeable definitions of consciousness. `X/x` is Taylor's notation. Here its precise consequence is that no local `x`, including a self-image, exhausts the determining `X` it makes legible.

Throughout this [whole knowing relation](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md), an achieved determination can disclose the circumstance through which it became known and return to that condition. The complete sequence keeps the Subject in relation to its differentiated world; its formal constructions retain their particular hypotheses and counted objects.

## #4

First-person presence is always lived through a circumstance. Body, language, memory, feeling, attention, judgment and tools participate in that circumstance. They can be investigated because they are determinate; being internal to a person does not make them identical with the Subject. Through [Objective Internality](C41-Objective-Internality.md), these means constitute the operative world in which something is available to know and act upon. Their mediation belongs to the lived relation between knower and known.

The second person makes the consequence unavoidable. I can know things about you and still have to hear your answer. Your presence is not another content I can produce by improving my image of you. Inclusion within the whole does not give my situated self possession of your relation to that whole. An [answering Other](../A27-Self-and-Other-Unity-without-Possession.md) can correct the account or change the terms through which I approached them. In the Watson–Gans–Levinas encounter, the face exceeds the egoic image held of it; my viewpoint meets someone whose response it cannot supply.

This carries ontological force. The order **Subject → objective internality → object** makes a determinable world available through the field of appearing, while a private ego remains a particular formation within it. In this [order of dependence](../A34-Idealism-Order-of-Dependence.md), subjective immediacy, mediating world and encountered object have different offices. Defined indefinability positively determines the subject-pole; its asymmetry concerns the present act and its appearances, beyond the incompleteness of a description.

Memory, self-model, report and internal organisation are determinate contents and operations. Their technical inspectability makes the mediating field increasingly explicit. Within a local inquiry, an interpreting agent functions as knower, its sources, memory, comparison rules and tools as means, and the addressed field as known. Within the containing person's inquiry, that complete apparatus itself occupies the means office. A further inspection can make the local determining centre known. These relative offices remain within Life / Mind: no accumulation of determinate objects converts those objects into the unobjectifiable subject-pole to which their determination is present.

## #5→0

Through [the eye's constitutive blindside](../../../symbolon/mytheme/worlds/frank-taylor/maya-eye-veil-frame-horizon/WHOLE.md#maya-eye-condition), an image of the organ becomes known while its present seeing remains the condition of that disclosure. A mirror, diagram or another observer can disclose more of the view's conditions. Each further disclosure is real and still appears through a situated act. The subject-pole cannot be recovered as an extra object that would complete the inventory, while the gained knowledge remains available for faithful use.

Return recognises the condition already involved in every portrait, judgment and attempt at recognition. The first-person force of *I am* remains, while its determinate descriptions become available for correction rather than being asked to stand as their own ground. [Recognition](C19-Pratyabhijna-Recognition.md) recovers that source relation through the acquired determination. In [integral zero's return](../A36-Advent-of-Integral-Zero.md), the achieved sign becomes Symbol: exact determination remains, now answerable to what it cannot own.

Through [[symbolon/episteme/etymologies/symbol-account-and-trust/WHOLE-FIELD|Symbol / Account / Trust]], a name discloses, an account makes disclosure answerable, and trust permits committed use without possession of the source. Their operational relation keeps their lexical histories distinct. In [[section-rooms/00-integral-threshold/movements/02-s01-p1-define-subject|defining the Subject]], the defining act remains present within the account it gives. At the [[section-rooms/07-instrument-returns/movements/47-s50-p4-idealism-horizon|idealist horizon]], the differentiated world and its means of appearing return to that presence. The account can be examined, corrected or fittingly retained; the next act inherits the warranted judgment while the source remains more than its description.
